timed: One-hour transition update; AoS writes object state, SoA end-to-end includes gather, aligned numeric update, and scatter.
Native Rust loop over preallocated packed buffers.
notTimed: FarmEngine construction, input derivation/feeding, full 24-hour tick, renderer, FFI and process startup.

timed: Projection of ID, weight and energy into one output object per animal; structuredClone of the AoS projection.
Node structuredClone transfer-list ownership handoff of preallocated numeric input and output buffers.
notTimed: Worker scheduling, message queue latency, browser postMessage and computation.

timed: JSON.stringify of the same AoS output projection.

codeComplexity.prototypeRepresentation: six aligned numeric buffers plus stable ID index

limitations: The checked-in baseline-pasture fixture provides the seed/configuration; its three-animal count is scaled to the supported benchmark populations. The one-hour transition input and expected output are generated from FarmEngine itself at active hour 7 and rest hour 22.
Native Rust measures the identical packed input in a pure kernel; it excludes JSON serialization, FFI, Worker queueing and process startup.
Heap/ArrayBuffer readings are process snapshots after GC; exact typed-buffer byte counts are the attributable memory result. JavaScript peak allocation counts are not instrumented.
Snapshot materialization projects stable ID, weight and energy, not every public FarmEngine snapshot field. JSON serialization separately measures this output projection.

decisionEvidence.rule: Keep AoS unless SoA end-to-end median is lower in every measured population/hour and wins at least 80% of counterbalanced paired samples in every row.
decisionEvidence.recommendation: Keep object-per-animal production state; the measured SoA path did not show repeatable end-to-end gains across all workloads.

decision: Keep object-per-animal production state; the measured SoA path did not show repeatable end-to-end gains across all workloads.
